chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: Snake Hips Tucker, Duke's film and playing shows behind him
summary: Barney Bigard's story of the film trouble and Cole backing him in shows.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Tell you what, let's go back about 20 years before that and pick up. Before we even do--I was going to ask you about Frankie Newton, but while we were taking a break, you mentioned about Snake Hips Tucker. Would you mind putting that on tape, it's a nice story.

No, because Barney Bigard told it to me. He said at that time, you know, God there was so much pressure that was going on then, you know, between the blacks and the whites, you know, especially white women and black men. That when Duke did some picture, I don't know what it was--
Maybe with Amos and Andy, way back there, yeah.

And 'Snake Hips' went out there and with those white girls throwing notes and all, and damn near knocked Duke out of the whole thing, whole picture and everything, you know. He was an ignorant boy, you know, and the gals out there liked him, you know, and he just went out there and almost threw the whole thing, open like that. The man said I don't care what you do, but damn, just don't be so open with it, at that day and time.
You said you used to play shows backing him?

Snake Hips? Oh yeah, I did a lot of shows. He was an act. You know. Willie Bryant with his band played for him, Benny Carter's band played for him, you know, at different times, oh yeah, I played for him a lot of times.
Did you get to know him at all?
Oh yeah, but not real intimate, you know, just knowing, 'Hey, Cozy; Hey, 'Snake Hips', how you doin?' One of those things, and See ya later, you know. Not intimate really.
Hips" Tucker, There was another Snake Hips around then, a very nice looking one. He never made it quite as big as this Earl. There was another one round there could do it just as well as he did.
